instructions: The night before: pour the 4 cups milk into a medium nonstick pot, off the heat. Add the 1/2 cup cornstarch and the 1/2 cup sugar, and whisk until the cornstarch is smooth.
Set the pot over medium heat and whisk until the sugar dissolves and the milk comes to a boil. Keep whisking so it doesn't stick to the bottom.
Turn the heat down to low and cook for 10 minutes, whisking often, until the pudding is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the 1 tsp rose water.
Pour the pudding into 4 bowls or jars. Let them cool on the counter for 30 minutes, then cover and refrigerate overnight.
In the morning, serve it cold straight from the fridge. Leftovers keep covered in the fridge for up to 5 days.
advance_prep_notes: make the pudding the night before and chill it overnight
method_notes: Lead is Salt and Sweet's Mahalabia (5.0 from 62), which thickens 4 cups of milk with 1/2 cup cornstarch and 1/2 cup sugar; Simply Lebanese uses 7 tablespoons cornstarch and chills 2 to 4 hours. The pistachio garnish and the orange blossom water are left out to keep it nut-free and simple. Both sources say fridge life is 2 to 5 days; the lead also says it freezes, but cornstarch puddings can turn watery, so no freezing is given here.
